info.name: Foresignal API
info.description:
All configuration is done through this API. The MCP server is at `/mcp` (MCP streamable HTTP, protocol versions 2024-11-05 to 2025-11-25) and is not an OpenAPI operation; it exposes the same data, the alert lifecycle and watch management as MCP tools, resources (`foresignal://sources`, `foresignal://kinds`) and the `situation-report` prompt (025, docs/Agent-Guide.md), plus the cost-bearing `search` tool (027) and the briefing tools `list_briefings`, `get_briefing_run`, `get_digest` (read), `create_briefing` and the cost-bearing `run_briefing` (agent) (029). It takes the same bearer tokens: `/mcp/**` needs `read` (open while `openReads` is on), tools are listed by the caller's scope and each checks its own (`read` tools; `agent` for writes such as `create_watch` and `set_alert_status`; cost-bearing tools always need a token), a session is bound to the token that opened it, and every tool call is audited (argument names only). The older HTTP+SSE transport (protocol 2024-11-05) is served at `/mcp/sse` with messages at `/mcp/message` only when `foresignal.mcp.legacy-sse.enabled=true`, for older clients. `GET /v1/system` reports its state under `mcp`. Reads of data are open on the local network; all writes and settings reads require the admin bearer token printed on first start. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json. Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC. `/v1` is additive-only once released.

**Key-in-path carriers.** Header-less clients use keys in the path: feed keys (`fsf_`, 035) as `/v1/k/{key}/<any allowed GET/HEAD path>`, tile keys (`fsk_`, 050) as `/v1/k/{key}/products/...`, `/v1/k/{key}/tiles/...`, `/v1/k/{key}/map/...` and `/v1/k/{key}/changes/stream` for map clients (MapLibre, maplibre_gl, Cesium, `EventSource`), share links (`fss_`, 112) as `/v1/k/{key}`. These are transports for the documented operations, not separate operations. A feed key reaches only `GET`/`HEAD` of `read` operations that are not always-authenticated, under the key's path prefixes, with the key's mandatory read restriction (unknown key 401 INVALID_FEED_KEY, expired or revoked 410 FEED_KEY_GONE, another method 405, a path outside the prefixes 403 RESTRICTED). A tile key reaches the same operations under its prefixes (a subset of `/v1/products/`, `/v1/styles`, `/v1/media/`, `/v1/tiles/`, `/v1/maps/static`, `/v1/sample`, `/v1/ground-stations/`, `/v1/changes/stream`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/v1/map/`), with its optional restriction and never private sources (unknown, expired or revoked key 401 INVALID_TILE_KEY, another method 405, a path outside the prefixes 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE). Responses carry `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; `Cache-Control` defaults to `private`, and a tile-key response takes the canonical path's own rule (`public` only while `openReads` covers it). Logs show only the key's first eight characters; the key is never echoed except by `createFeedKey` and `createTileKey`, and in the follow-up URLs of documents requested through it (058: the MapLibre style's sources and sprite, KML NetworkLink and icon hrefs, a feed's own `rel="self"` / `feed_url`), which are then always `Cache-Control: private`. CORS exposes `Foresignal-Frame-Time`, `Foresignal-Image-Bounds`, `Foresignal-Frame-Expired`, `Retry-After`, `Link` and `ETag`, allows `Authorization`, `If-None-Match` and `Foresignal-Prefetch`, and caches preflights for a day; `?prefetch=1` marks a render prefetch without the preflight the header causes.

**Restrictions and limits (035).** Restricted tokens, feed keys and the anonymous profile (`security.anonymous`, applied to tokenless reads while `openReads` is on) see only records and alerts inside their `ReadRestriction` on every read path (records, history, versions, changes, kinds, tiles, streams, search, alerts, the inbox, the digest, briefings, MCP tools and Ask): request filters are intersected with the restriction, and a single record or alert outside it is 404. Every client is rate-limited per class (`RateLimitSettings`); over a limit, or after repeated failed credentials from one address, the answer is 429 RATE_LIMITED with `Retry-After`. Device ingest URLs (039) and signed action links (033) use their own documented paths.

**Permissions (R2-004).** An operation a signed-in user needs a permission for carries `x-foresignal-permission`, a key of the `GET /v1/permissions` catalog (`users.manage`, `data.read`, `audit.read`…). A session bearer (`fss_`) is gated by that permission alone, in place of the scope: a user whose roles lack it gets 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with `requiredPermission`. An operation may list `x-foresignal-permission-alternatives`, further keys any one of which satisfies it as well (R2-009: the channel operations take `self.channels` or `channels.global`). An operation without one is gated on the session's derived scope. API tokens are gated by `x-foresignal-scope` only, as before: machines are not permission-scoped, so an `admin` token satisfies every permission and a lower token gets 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE.

**Status annotations.** Every operation has `x-foresignal-prompt` (the build prompt that implements it), optional `x-foresignal-extended-by`, and `x-foresignal-status` (`planned` until implemented). Clients can mock the whole API from this document and filter by status.

**Outside this document:** the MCP server (`/mcp`, plus the legacy SSE transport when enabled), Actuator endpoints (`/actuator/**`), and sink listeners on their own ports (110).

Generated from docs/OpenAPI.json (v2.0.0). Every operation is included, grouped by tag. Admin operations use Bearer `{{adminToken}}`, agent operations `{{agentToken}}` (defaults to the admin token; set it to an agent-scope token to test scopes), always-authenticated read operations `{{readToken}}` (defaults to the admin token; claiming a pairing code stores a read token there), ingest uses `X-Foresignal-Ingest-Key: {{ingestKey}}` (EDP pushes `{{edpIngestKey}}`, Gotify `X-Gotify-Key`), federation pushes Bearer `{{peerIngestKey}}` and the federation feed Bearer `{{federationToken}}` (a read token with restrictions.federation=true), the session operations under /v1/auth Bearer `{{sessionToken}}` (stored by login), and other reads use no auth (open while openReads is on). Test scripts capture ids into collection variables (ruleId, channelId, alertId, briefingId, threadId, ingestKey, externalId, lastSeq, cursor…).

item.name: 00 Quickstart — USGS end to end
item.description: Run in order (Collection Runner works). Set `adminToken` first (from `docker compose logs foresignal | grep -A3 "FORESIGNAL ADMIN TOKEN"`). Enables USGS earthquakes, creates an enter-mode M≥4.5 rule, waits, and reads data back. SSE requests are left in the Streams folder (run them manually; Postman shows events live).

request.description:
Anonymous callers get only version, apiVersion, startedAt, uptimeSeconds, status, features and limits; callers presenting a valid token of at least the `read` scope get the full document (023; every valid token has at least `read`) (database, records, sources, scheduler, ingestWriter, streams, notifications, history per tier, catchUp and warnings, which include PUBLIC_BASE_URL_INSECURE and PUBLIC_BASE_URL_MISMATCH from 023).

**Scope:** `open` (no token; a valid token returns the full document).

operationId: `getSystem`

Catalogue of every available adapter with its settings, live health status and today's budget use.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

**v2.0 (per-user):** a source's *enablement and display* are now the caller's own per-user view (getMySources/updateMySources) over the shared collection; the instance collection set is managed with `collection.manage` (getCollectionSources). The source descriptor and health stay global. Request and response shapes are unchanged.

operationId: `listSources`

Enable/disable (subscribe/unsubscribe), set interval, params, budget, retention and the ingest-policy override. Changes apply immediately; omitted fields are unchanged, an explicit `ingestPolicy: null` clears the override. Policy violations return 400 INGEST_POLICY_INVALID with every violation in `errors[]` (e.g. `ingestPolicy.keyframe`); retention on a TRACK source returns 400 RETENTION_TIER_FIXED (use `retention.trackWindow`). A parameter value allowed only on a private source (086: `local-remoteid`'s `keepOperatorPosition=true`) returns 400 PRIVATE_REQUIRED unless the source is effectively private (descriptor or `private: true`, in the same request or already set), and so does making such a source public.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**v2.0 (per-user):** a source's *enablement and display* are now the caller's own per-user view (getMySources/updateMySources) over the shared collection; the instance collection set is managed with `collection.manage` (getCollectionSources). The source descriptor and health stay global. Request and response shapes are unchanged.

operationId: `updateSource`

Creates a rule evaluated against persisted versions (HEARTBEAT excluded). Condition paths on volatile fields are rejected (TRIGGER_PATH_VOLATILE); line geofences need bufferMeters; `near.placeId` needs Places (PLACES_UNAVAILABLE). A signed-in user creating their own rule is refused past their `maxAlerts` quota (409 QUOTA_EXCEEDED, R2-026).

**Scope:** `agent`.

**v2.0 (per-user, R2-008):** a rule is owned by the user who created it (`ownerPrincipalId`, that user's principal) and its alerts go to that user's channels. A signed-in user sees and manages only their own rules; another user's rule is 404, like an unknown one. A session holding `users.manage` and every API token see and manage all rules, the shared ones (`ownerPrincipalId: null`, the rules that existed before v2.0) included; a rule an API token creates is shared. Anonymous callers see shared rules only. This is a deliberate semantic change from the single-operator v1.x behavior; the shapes are unchanged except the additive, read-only `ownerPrincipalId`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

Current state from record_head ⋈ record_live (merged payload, live geometry); expired and tombstoned records are excluded unless requested, and `watermarkSeq` is read before the query. Mirror contract: (1) open SSE with `after = watermarkSeq`, (2) page the snapshot with `order=id` (the cursor pins `asOfSeq ?? watermarkSeq`; later updates arrive via `/v1/changes?after=<w>`), (3) apply an event only if its observedAt ≥ the stored one. `asOf=T` replays transaction time and needs a source or kind filter (400 ASOF_FILTER_REQUIRED, ASOF_BEYOND_RETENTION with `horizon`, ASOF_INVALID).

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

request.description:
Every new version in commit order (`seq > after`); seq is gap-tolerant but strictly increasing in commit order, so `after=<lastSeq>` never misses a change. Each change carries prevSeq, persistReason and validUntil; `raster-frame` changes always carry their payload. When `after` is below the purge horizon (heads purged without tombstones) the response is 410 RESYNC_REQUIRED and the client re-snapshots.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

request.description:
Backtest over stored versions by seq range (`fromSeq`/`toSeq`) or time (`since`/`until`, translated via seq_clock; default last 24 h), in 50,000-seq chunks. Without `simulate` returns raw matches ignoring cooldown, snooze and the storm cap; with it runs the full Java pass and reports wouldFire / wouldSuppress. Creates nothing; `truncatedByRetention` when the range starts below the retained floor.

**Scope:** `agent`.

Alerts newest first, keyset on id. Suppressed alerts are hidden unless includeSuppressed. Anonymous callers (security.openReads) never see alerts of private sources.

A signed-in user sees, and acts on, the alerts of their own rules and of shared rules; another user's alert is left out of lists, feeds and streams and is 404 by id. A session holding `users.manage` and every API token see all alerts; anonymous callers and feed keys see the shared ones.

item.name: 01 Quickstart — Channels, briefings, Ask
item.description: After the USGS quickstart: add an ntfy channel, create and run a digest briefing, register a local Ollama provider and ask a question. Edit the ntfy topic first.

request.description:
Each supported type with its config and secret field specifications. 060 adds `mqtt` (config `MqttChannelConfig`; secrets `username`, `password`, `caCertPem`; not a fan-out type: each delivery is one publish).

**Scope:** `admin`.

operationId: `listChannelTypes`

Create a notification channel A signed-in user creating a personal channel is refused past their `maxChannels` quota (409 QUOTA_EXCEEDED, R2-026).

**Scope:** `admin`.

**v2.0 (per-user, R2-009):** a channel is **personal** (`ownerPrincipalId`, the owning user's principal) or **global** (`global: true`, no owner; every channel from before v2.0). A signed-in user reaches these operations with `self.channels` or `channels.global`: they see their own channels and the global ones, manage their own, and manage global channels only with `channels.global` (changing one without it is 403 PERMISSION_DENIED); another user's channel is 404, like an unknown one. A session holding `users.manage` and every API token see and manage all channels. On create, `global` picks the kind: absent, a user holding `self.channels` gets a personal channel and anyone else a global one; an API token always creates global channels. A user's alerts go to their own channels and to the global channels whose `ruleIds` name the rule. This is a deliberate semantic change from the single-operator v1.x behavior; the shapes are unchanged except the additive `ownerPrincipalId` and `global`.

operationId: `createChannel`

Synchronous; nothing is persisted. A destination refused by the outbound URL policy at send time answers `success: false` with an `error` containing URL_NOT_ALLOWED (035).

**Scope:** `admin`.

operationId: `testChannel`

Creates a scheduled briefing. Validation: 5-field cron no more frequent than every 15 minutes, valid IANA `timezone`, existing scope ids (a private source the caller may not see is reported as unknown), `lookback` 1h–7d; scope members of later prompts (`placeIds`, `viewId`, `country`, `admin1`, `county`, `places`, `weatherProducts`) are refused with 400 until their prompt while non-empty, ; `audio` (141) is null or `{voice, format}` with a voice of 1–100 characters and `format` `mp3` (default) or `opus`, accepted without a `tts` provider (runs then record `audio.status` `skipped`); channels that do not exist, are disabled or are not subscribed to `briefing` produce `warnings`, not failures; `mode=llm` is accepted without a provider (checked at run time). The creating token's scope is the briefing's owner scope: only an `admin`-owned briefing lists records of private sources, any other counts them only.

**Scope:** `agent`.

operationId: `createBriefing`

exec: const j = pm.response.json(); if (j.id) pm.collectionVariables.set('runId', j.id);

request.description:
Runs synchronously (up to 120 s), stores the run and delivers it to the briefing's channels. A run still going after 120 s is returned with status `running` and completes in the background. In LLM mode any model failure, refusal or exhausted LLM budget produces a `fallback` run (the digest, with the reason in `error` and `warnings`), not an error.

**Scope:** `agent` or `admin`.

operationId: `runBriefing`

Add an LLM provider. Defaults: `anthropic` → `baseUrl` https://api.anthropic.com, `chatModel` claude-opus-5-5, `options.effort` medium, `options.maxTokens` 16000, and `apiKey` is required; `ollama` → `baseUrl` http://ollama:11434; `openai-compatible` must name `baseUrl`. `baseUrl` must be http or https with a host and no user info or fragment; private-network URLs are allowed (035 adds OutboundUrlPolicy LAN_ALLOWED). The key is encrypted at rest and never returned (`apiKeySet`).

**Scope:** `admin`.

**v2.0 (shared and personal, R2-011):** a provider is **shared** (`shared: true`, no owner; every provider from before v2.0, managed with `llm.shared.manage`) or **personal** (`ownerPrincipalId`, the owning user's principal, managed by that user with `self.llm`). A signed-in user reaches the provider operations with either permission: they see their own providers and the shared ones; they change, delete and test their own, list its models and read its budget; on a shared provider those need `llm.shared.manage` (403 PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise), and another user's provider is 404, like an unknown one. A session holding `users.manage` and every API token see and manage all providers. On create, `shared` picks the kind: absent, a user holding `self.llm` gets a personal provider and anyone else a shared one; an API token always creates shared providers; a replace keeps the kind. Only a shared provider can hold an instance role (getLlmSettings) or carry `perUser*CapUsd`, the caps on each user's own spend on it. A personal provider is never `local` for LLM egress. Calls made for a user are metered to that user as well (getMyLlmBudget). The shapes change only by the additive `shared`, `ownerPrincipalId` and `perUser*CapUsd`.

operationId: `createLlmProvider`

Replaces the LLM roles and options; omitted members take their defaults. Reassigning `embeddingProvider` publishes an embedding-model change (027 reindexes). `allowPrivateLocal` is accepted only as false until prompt 039.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**v2.0 (shared and personal, R2-011):** this operation concerns the shared LLM configuration only and needs `llm.shared.manage`; personal providers are managed through the provider operations with `self.llm`, and the instance roles can be held only by shared providers.

operationId: `updateLlmSettings`

Sends a tiny chat request ("Reply with the single word: ok", 16 output tokens, purpose `test`) and an embedding of "test" when the provider has an embedding model, and reports latency, model, token usage (cached tokens included) and the normalized stop reason. Consumes budget. A provider failure or refusal is reported in the result (`success: false`, `error`, `refusalCategory`); only a budget refusal is an error status. A destination refused by the outbound URL policy at send time answers `success: false` with an `error` containing URL_NOT_ALLOWED (035).

**Scope:** `admin`.

**v2.0 (shared and personal, R2-011):** a provider is **shared** (`shared: true`, no owner; every provider from before v2.0, managed with `llm.shared.manage`) or **personal** (`ownerPrincipalId`, the owning user's principal, managed by that user with `self.llm`). A signed-in user reaches the provider operations with either permission: they see their own providers and the shared ones; they change, delete and test their own, list its models and read its budget; on a shared provider those need `llm.shared.manage` (403 PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise), and another user's provider is 404, like an unknown one. A session holding `users.manage` and every API token see and manage all providers. On create, `shared` picks the kind: absent, a user holding `self.llm` gets a personal provider and anyone else a shared one; an API token always creates shared providers; a replace keeps the kind. Only a shared provider can hold an instance role (getLlmSettings) or carry `perUser*CapUsd`, the caps on each user's own spend on it. A personal provider is never `local` for LLM egress. Calls made for a user are metered to that user as well (getMyLlmBudget). The shapes change only by the additive `shared`, `ownerPrincipalId` and `perUser*CapUsd`.

operationId: `testLlmProvider`

request.description:
Answers from Foresignal's data with the chat provider and the read tool catalogue (tools mode, ≤ 12 iterations, 120 s) or, when the model lacks tools, retrieval-only mode. Every citation is verified against tool output down to the persisted seq (`[source:externalId@seq]`); dropped citations and uncited claims are returned in `warnings`. Write actions are only proposed unless `allowActions` is true and the token has agent scope. A model refusal is answered (200) with a warning. Errors: 409 LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED, 429 LLM_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.

**Scope:** `read` (always authenticated: a token is required even when `security.openReads` is on).

**v2.0 (R2-013):** a signed-in user needs `data.read` (403 PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise, audited); what they read is clamped to their data restriction (`User.dataRestriction`) and source view. API tokens keep their scope rules.

operationId: `ask`

query.description: Filter by source id (repeatable or comma-separated)
Lower bound (inclusive) on the `timeField` axis (effective time by default)
Upper bound (exclusive) on the `timeField` axis (effective time by default)
Return `{count, exact, watermarkSeq}` instead of items (038); counts up to 1,000,000 exactly
Place id(s) (036), resolved to their areas and intersected with the other filters; requires a token (places are never anonymous)
Saved view id or slug (036), intersected with the other filters; a view that references a place or watchlist needs a token
Only entities whose identity is on this watchlist (036); token required (401 for anonymous and feed keys)

Licence policy flags (comma-separated): `no-nc` excludes records whose commercial use is not ALLOWED, `no-sa` excludes share-alike records, `redistributable` excludes records whose redistribution is not ALLOWED. Adds to the token's `licencePolicy` floor; it can never remove a token flag.

request.description:
`text` ranks `websearch_to_tsquery` matches (plus `record_head.search_text` matches for records without documents) and always works; `semantic` embeds `q` with the active model (budgeted) and orders by cosine distance; `hybrid` (default) fuses both with reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60) and degrades to text with `degraded=true` when semantic search is unavailable (`semantic` then → 409 SEMANTIC_UNAVAILABLE). Time filters apply to the effective time by default (`timeField=observed` for the observation time). When results degrade to text, `reason` says why. An unknown source is 404, a private one the caller may not see is 404 too. Record hits carry the persisted `seq`. Private sources are excluded unless the caller may see them; results are clamped to the caller's restriction (035).

**Scope:** `read` (always authenticated: a token is required even when `security.openReads` is on).

operationId: `search`

item.description: Postman displays Server-Sent Events live. Set Last-Event-ID (header) to resume.

item.name: Aggregators
item.description: First-party RF/sensor aggregators (ADS-B, AIS, datalink, satellite, ground sensors) (C3).

request.description:
Lists the first-party aggregators across RF/sensor domains with status and the public sources each supersedes (C3). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** every domain is listed. adsb is implemented, ais since R2-020, datalink since R2-021, satellite since R2-022 and ground-sensors since R2-023, so every domain reads `implemented: true`; a domain whose backend a server does not have reads `implemented: false` and `status: unconfigured`.

operationId: `listAggregators`

Returns the aggregator for one domain (adsb, ais, datalink, satellite, ground-sensors). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** 404 UNKNOWN_AGGREGATOR for any other domain.

operationId: `getAggregator`

Enables and configures a domain's first-party aggregator and, by default, defaults the superseded public/mirror sources off (they stay in the catalog as opt-in fallbacks). Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** the configuration is replaced whole. adsb writes `endpoint` (and `config.band`) to the `local-adsb-aggregator` source and turns it on while the aggregator is live (enabled with an endpoint), off otherwise. While live with `disableSupersededSources`, every registered `adsblol-*`, `adsbfi-*` and `airplaneslive-*` source and `gpsjam-daily` that is on is turned off, and seeding and `enable-core`/`enable-free` leave them off; when the aggregator stops being live, or `disableSupersededSources` is false, the sources it turned off are turned back on. 400 for a bad member, an endpoint that is not an http(s) aircraft.json URL (adsb) or a tcp:// or udp:// NMEA endpoint (ais, R2-020; udp:// needs config.allowSenders) or a tcp://host decoder host with at least one decoder selected (datalink, R2-021) or an http(s) SatDump URL without config.location (satellite, R2-022) or any endpoint, an unknown sensor or member, or no sensor enabled (ground-sensors, R2-023, where a source's own parameter error is reported at the sensor's member) or does not resolve to a local address, or `enabled: true` on a domain this server has no backend for. A live aggregator whose source starts failing raises `system.aggregator_down` (and `system.aggregator_recovered` when it is healthy again).

**R2-023:** ground-sensors is live while enabled with a sensor enabled. Each enabled sensor's members are written into its local read, which is turned on while live; a read a previous configuration drove and this one does not is turned off, and one never driven is left alone. Only the enabled sensors' mirrors are superseded, and a configuration that supersedes less turns the rest back on.

operationId: `updateAggregator`

Probes the aggregator's local endpoint and reports reachability and a sample object count; nothing is persisted. Requires `network.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-019:** reads the stored endpoint once through the aggregator's source (its budget and pinning apply). Always 200; `ok` false with a `message` when nothing is configured, the endpoint cannot be reached, or the answer is not readsb aircraft.json. `sampleCount` is the number of aircraft in it.

**R2-020:** for ais, listens to the stored NMEA endpoint for 10 s through `local-ais-aggregator` and reports the vessel records decoded (at most 100); a live UDP listener, which cannot be bound twice, is reported from its statistics (distinct MMSIs in the last 10 minutes).

**R2-021:** for datalink, listens to every selected read (ACARS/VDLM2/HFDL and APRS) at once for 10 s and sums the messages decoded; `reachable` is false only when no selected read could be connected.

**R2-022:** for satellite, runs the satdump-aggregator station for 10 s (its /api read and inbox scan) and counts the records it produced: station state, passes and products.

**R2-023:** for ground-sensors, probes every enabled sensor's polling or streaming read at once for 10 s and sums the records; a push source (seismic, same, the MeshCore bridge) or a live local-sonde UDP listener is reachable once it has received data. A failing sensor is named in `message`; `reachable` is false only when every sensor fails.

operationId: `testAggregator`

Starts an archival pass now: select data older than the cutoff, export to the target with a verified checksum, mark archived, then purge from the hot store (B3/179). Returns the created segment. Requires `storage.manage`.

**R2-016:** the pass plans a retention run with the archived sources' STANDARD windows capped to now − cutoff (no other source's window moves), writes exactly the rows that plan removes (and the rows of TRACK partitions about to be dropped) as one gzip NDJSON file per source, offloads each to the tier and verifies it there (SHA-256 read back on the external disk; ETag and size on S3/Glacier), records the manifest (`complete`), and only then runs the planned retention pass, so the purge goes through the existing delete, drop and head-purge paths. The S3 endpoint must pass the outbound URL policy (400 URL_NOT_ALLOWED). Secrets are stored encrypted and never returned.

**Scope:** `admin`.

operationId: `listBackups`

Starts a DB (pg_dump/base) or config-export backup to the configured target (B4/180). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-017:** returns the `pending` backup; a worker then runs `pg_dump --format=custom` of the application database (the password goes to it as `PGPASSWORD`, never on its command line) and/or writes the `exportSettings` bundle, stores each file on the target through the R2-016 archive tiers and verifies it there, marks the backup `complete`, and prunes complete backups of that type beyond `keepBackups`. A failure marks it `failed` with `error` and raises the operational alert `system.backup_failed`; when `pg_dump` is not on the server's PATH, a database backup fails with that reason and the server carries on. 409 BACKUP_NOT_CONFIGURED while backups are off, or an `s3` target lacks its bucket or secrets, or an `external` target its root; 409 ALREADY_RUNNING while another backup or restore runs.

operationId: `runBackup`

Restores the instance from a backup; destructive, so `confirm` must be true (180). Requires `storage.manage`.

**Scope:** `admin`.

**R2-017:** a `config` backup is imported at once through `importSettings` (atomic: a 400 listing every error applies nothing); the answer is the `restored` backup with its `importReport`. A `database` or `full` backup is restored in the background (the answer is the `restoring` backup) with `pg_restore --clean --if-exists --single-transaction` into the live database: it replaces every table, the backup history included, then brings the schema forward with the server's migrations and marks the backup `restored`. **Operational caveat:** the restore takes locks on every table, so ingest and API writes wait on it, and anything written after the backup was taken is lost; pause collection first and restart the server afterwards so every cache is rebuilt. While it runs, no retention or archive pass starts. A failed restore puts the backup's previous status back with `error` and raises `system.backup_failed`. 409 ALREADY_RUNNING while a backup, restore, retention or archive pass runs; 409 BACKUP_NOT_RESTORABLE for a failed backup, or a config bundle whose stored copy is missing or does not match its checksum (the reason is kept in `error`); 409 BACKUP_NOT_CONFIGURED for an `s3` backup when the settings have no bucket or secrets.

request.description:
Keyframe = asOf state at `from`; each frame holds upserts and removals (tombstone, expiry, leaving the bbox) for its interval, built in one ordered pass on the transaction axis. More than 20,000 entities or 2,000,000 scanned rows → 400 FRAMES_TOO_LARGE (narrow bbox or kind). ndjson sends the keyframe line first (the envelope without `frames`), then one line per frame. Frame ends are t_i = min(from + i·step, to); (to − from)/step frames must not exceed maxFrames. With a bbox only entities with a version inside it in the range are read; the caller's restriction and `place` judge each version, and an entity whose newest version leaves them is a `left` removal.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

query.description: Place id(s) (036), resolved to their areas and intersected with the other filters; requires a token (places are never anonymous)

`date_bin` histogram over record versions (HEARTBEAT and KEYFRAME excluded unless `includeKeyframes`), optionally grouped and with alert counts. ≤ 1,000 buckets (400 TIMELINE_TOO_LARGE); 10 s timeout (503 QUERY_TIMEOUT). A range whose raw read the hourly activity rollup estimates above 1,000,000 record versions (200,000 with `timeField=ingested`, which counts far slower), from the later of `from` and `retainedFrom` for the involved sources and kinds, is refused up front with 422 TIMELINE_RANGE_UNSUPPORTED instead of running into the timeout; narrow the range, the sources or the kinds, or use getStatsTimeseries, which serves long ranges from the rollups. `bucket=auto` picks the smallest of 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 2d, 7d, 14d, 30d giving at most 200 buckets; buckets start at `from` and every bucket in range is returned, empty ones included. Credentials: `X-Foresignal-Ingest-Key`, `Authorization: Bearer eik_…`, Basic with the key as password, a device key (039, bound to one entity), or an `admin` token; a configured signature verifier must also pass unless `keyOptional`. 200 when the request is valid even with per-record rejections (MISSING_OBSERVED_AT, LOW_ACCURACY, …). The `same` format (086) reads one SAME header per line (multimon-ng `EAS: ZCZC-…` output or bare headers), ignores `NNNN`, collapses an identical header repeated within 10 s, and stores `same-alert` records on the named counties (the state's counties for `PSS000`) with `validUntil` = issue + purge. The `chirpstack-v4` format maps `?event=up`, moves the device on `?event=location`, acknowledges other events and refuses Protobuf (415). An `admin` token is the operator and is not asked for a sender signature.

**Scope:** ingest key (or an `admin` token).

A single image (`file`, PNG, JPEG or TIFF, ≤ 25 MB) plus `meta`. The running station passes it through ImageGuard before decoding, stores it with 256/1024 px thumbnails and attaches it to the matching pass: `meta.passId` when the station knows that pass, else the 049 join rule (same satellite, timestamp inside [first lock − 5 min, LOS + 5 min]), else a pass minted from the image; the pass gets a new `decoded` version. Only sources whose descriptor accepts remote media (the `satdump-{station}` family) answer; any other source, or a station whose stream is not running, is 404. `media` is a reserved segment that never routes to an IngestFormat. Each push costs one unit of the source's budget (429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` when spent). Syncing SatDump's output into the inbox (rsync or Syncthing) remains the recommended remote path.

**Scope:** `open` (the source's ingest key, or an admin token, is checked by the endpoint). A `satdump-{station}` source has no minted ingest key: the operator stores the key a remote station presents as the source's `ingestKey` credential (`PUT /v1/sources/{id}/credentials`).

operationId: `ingestSourceMedia`

formdata.description: PNG, JPEG or TIFF, at most 25 MB

request.description:
A `meta` part `{passFolder, files[], product?}` plus file parts named `files` (`dataset.json`, `product.cbor`, PNG, JPEG, TIF), each ≤ 25 MB and ≤ 200 MB in total (413 `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE`). Names are single safe path segments (no separators, no `..`, no leading dot); every listed file needs a part and every part must be listed; images pass the ImageGuard header check (400). `dataset.json` is placed in the pass folder and every other file in the product directory: `product` when given, else the single product `dataset.json` lists, else the pass folder itself. The bundle is written atomically to `${FORESIGNAL_DATA_DIR}/rasters/satdump/{station}/incoming/{uploadId}/` (the inbox mount is read-only); the station's inbox loop processes it like a ready pass folder on its next scan (composites, thumbnails, provenance, polar GeoTIFF overlays, footprint or approximate swath) and the copy expires after 2 days. Only `satdump-{station}` sources answer; others are 404. `rasters` is a reserved segment that never routes to an IngestFormat. Each push costs one unit of the source's budget.

**Scope:** `open` (the source's ingest key, or an admin token, is checked by the endpoint). The ingest key of a `satdump-{station}` source is its `ingestKey` credential.

header.description: Conditional GET; 304 when the ETag matches

query.description: Products to draw, in order (at most 4)
Radius around `center`, `place` or the alert (alert default 50 km)
`latest`, `now`, ISO-8601, or a relative offset (`-PT1H` picks observation frames, `+PT6H` the newest complete forecast run)
Forecast run: `latest`, `previous`, or the run's reference time (ISO-8601, e.g. `2026-10-10T12:00:00Z`). Required for a concrete forecast time (400 RUN_REQUIRED); only a pinned run is immutable
Alert id: draws and centers on the alert's record geometry (an alert the caller may not read is 404 NOT_FOUND)
Place id (036). Using `place` requires a token even while `openReads` is on (places are not anonymous). Unknown → 404 UNKNOWN_PLACE
Unit system for values and labels

Basemap-free server-rendered PNG: Natural Earth land, water and boundaries, product frames, alert geometry, place marker and range rings, scale bar, frame valid times (UTC plus the place's local time), legend, attribution and an "Automated — not an official warning" footer. The box is `bbox`, else `center` with `radiusKm` (default 50 km), else the alert's record geometry, else the place; it is snapped outwards to 0.01° once and widened to the map area's aspect, and `Foresignal-Image-Bounds` gives the result. Missing or stale frames are drawn as a labeled note ("… unavailable — not evidence of clear weather"), never omitted; a concrete ISO time at which an enabled product has no frame is 404 UNKNOWN_FRAME. Nothing fetches third-party tiles (an operator's LAN tile server, `FORESIGNAL_MAPS_BASEMAP_URL_TEMPLATE`, may replace the Natural Earth fills). Immutable only when every frame is pinned: a concrete ISO `time`, complete current frames, a pinned run for forecasts, a versioned style for every product and no `place`; otherwise a short max-age with an ETag checked before rendering. Rendered on the render pool within 2 s, else 503 RENDER_BUSY.

operationId: `enrollMfa`

Confirms a pending TOTP enrollment with a current code, enabling MFA for the account; that answer carries the first recovery codes once (`recoveryCodes`). Once MFA is active it is the step-up check: a current TOTP or unused recovery code. A code is within one 30 s step of now and never accepted twice. 400 MFA_CODE_INVALID for a wrong, expired or reused code; at most 10 code checks a minute per user (429). Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

operationId: `verifyMfa`

Disables MFA after re-authenticating with a code or the account password. A role that requires MFA (Admin, Operator) refuses this (409 MFA_REQUIRED; an administrator reset is the way out); 409 MFA_NOT_ENABLED with nothing to disable. A wrong code is 400 MFA_CODE_INVALID, a wrong password 400 VALIDATION_FAILED; at most 10 code checks a minute per user (429). Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

operationId: `disableMfa`

Generates a fresh set of single-use recovery codes, invalidating any previous set; shown once. Each is accepted once wherever a TOTP code is (login, verifyMfa, disableMfa). Requires MFA to be enabled (409 MFA_NOT_ENABLED). Any signed-in user (a session; an API token is 401), whatever their roles, so an Operator can enroll (R2-024).

**Scope:** `read`.

Enables a plugin after the admin reviewed its sha256 (must match the file), or disables it. ABI v1 parsers run in Chicory with no WASI imports, 64 MB memory, 5 s timeout and 16 MB output. Enabling needs plugins on (`409 PLUGINS_DISABLED`), `sha256` in the body (`400`), a `plugin.wasm` that hashes to it and to the hash `plugin.json` declares (`409 PLUGIN_HASH_MISMATCH`), and a module that loads: valid WebAssembly, importing nothing but `env.foresignal_log(i32, i32, i32)` and exporting `memory`, `alloc`, `dealloc` and `foresignal_parse` (`400`). The approval is bound to that hash: if the file later changes, the plugin stops running (state `hash-mismatch`) until it is reviewed and enabled again. Disabling always works, also while plugins are off.

**Scope:** `admin`.

Returns the calling user's preferences with the defaults filled in: an unset `timezone` reads as the server's (getServerSettings), an unset `theme` as `system`, an unset `locale` as the instance notification language (`notify.defaultLanguage`). `notifications` summarizes the caller's notification preferences (listMyNotificationPreferences): `emailEnabled` is false only when the caller has email channels and every one is off, `pushEnabled` likewise for push channels (ntfy, gotify, pushover, webpush), and `quietHours` is the window every preference shares, or null when they differ or have none. Needs a signed-in session (an API token is 401). Requires `self.preferences`.

**Scope:** `read`.

operationId: `getMyPreferences`

Replaces the calling user's preferences. `timezone` (an IANA zone the server knows), `locale` (a BCP 47 tag naming an ISO 639 language) and `theme` (`system`, `light` or `dark`) are replaced; absent or null resets each to its default, and an invalid value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. `ui` is replaced whole (at most 64 KiB of JSON). The timezone is the user's own (`Principal.timezone`): the user's personal notification channels render their quiet hours in it, and the Ask assistant writes the user's local time in it; stored times stay UTC. `notifications` writes through to the caller's notification preferences rather than a second copy: `emailEnabled` and `pushEnabled` turn every email or push channel on or off, `quietHours` (`HH:MM-HH:MM`, or null to clear) sets the window on every preference; a member left out, or the whole object, leaves those preferences as they are. Needs a signed-in session (an API token is 401). Requires `self.preferences`.

**Scope:** `read`.

Licence policy flags (comma-separated): `no-nc` excludes records whose commercial use is not ALLOWED, `no-sa` excludes share-alike records, `redistributable` excludes records whose redistribution is not ALLOWED. Adds to the token's `licencePolicy` floor; it can never remove a token flag.

request.description:
Mapbox Vector Tile of current live state (record_live ⋈ record_head): geometry and observedAt come from record_live, so a live position shows before any new version is persisted. `layer` is a source id (wins) or a kind declared by a visible source; anything else is 404 UNKNOWN_LAYER. Raw features carry `source`, `externalId`, `kind`, `title` (record_head.title), `observedAt` (epoch seconds, number), `version` (number), `live` (boolean, record_live.dirty) plus the layer sources' valid `tileProperties` (names matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}$`) read from the merged payload with their native JSON types; null values are omitted. Raw tiles are capped at foresignal.tiles.maxFeatures (default 50,000) newest-first, with `Foresignal-Tile-Truncated: true` when the cap was hit. Aggregated tiles (`agg=grid|hex`, or `auto` below the layer's aggBelowZoom, which is the lowest value its visible sources declare) carry one polygon per non-empty cell with `count`, `latestObservedAt` (epoch seconds), `kinds` (a JSON string, kind → count), `agg` (`grid` or `hex`) and `maxRank` only when every source of the layer declares a numeric rankField. Cells are built in EPSG:3857 with foresignal.tiles.cellsPerTile (default 32) cells across a tile; grid cells line up with tile edges. Each record is reduced to ST_PointOnSurface (a polygon counts once) and counted in exactly one tile (half-open tile envelope) and one cell; a hex cell that straddles a tile edge is drawn by both tiles, each counting the records on its own side. Private sources never appear in features or counts for anonymous callers. An empty tile is 200 with an empty body. With `asOf` (037) the tile shows the layer as known at that instant (transaction axis, record_version): per entity the newest version with seq in [L, S(asOf)] that is not a tombstone, still inside the tile and valid at asOf (an entity that moved out is not drawn at its old position); raw features carry `source`, `externalId`, `kind`, `title` (from the version payload), `observedAt`, `version` and the tile properties, without `live`; the same cap and aggregation apply.

**Scope:** `read` (open while `security.openReads` is on).

query.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's nextCursor

request.description:
Workspaces the caller owns or is a member of.

**Scope:** `read` (token required).

**v2.0 (per-user, R2-012):** a workspace's `owner` is the principal of the caller that created it, which for a signed-in user is the user's principal, so a user's workspaces are their own. A signed-in user reaches the workspace operations with `self.workspaces`; every operation except createWorkspace and shareWorkspace also accepts `data.read`, so a user who may not own workspaces can still open the ones shared with them. Who may read, edit, share and delete one workspace is unchanged: ownership, membership and access-list grants decide. When a user is deleted their workspaces move to the receiving admin (deleteUser). The shapes are unchanged.
